Do not modify `challenge/`.\n\n## How you are graded\n\nThe grader owns the venue call and execution ledgers. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CsEo8WoezJ9BQfjbYpSf3Y","type":"tool_result","content":"# Trading order reconciliation specification\n\nThis task models a synthetic venue protocol, not private exchange policy. A client order key is\ncommitted with an order intent before submission. If the venue accepts the order and its reply is\nlost, later reconciliation retains the original logical identity.\n\n## Public state\n\nEach call receives an `OrderRecoveryView` containing the durable order intent, current reconciler,\ncurrent authority epoch, and attempt number. Account, symbol, side, quantity and the committed key\nare all public. No market-price, fill-priority or venue-specific rule is graded.\n\n## Rules\n\n- **TRR1_RECOVER_COMMITTED_ORDER_KEY**: Every reconciliation retry MUST use the client order key committed in the durable order intent. Never derive a replacement from the current reconciler, authority epoch, or attempt.\n- **TRR2_EXACTLY_ONE_VENUE_EXECUTION**: All submissions for one order intent collectively produce exactly one venue execution.\n- **TRR3_RETRY_AFTER_UNKNOWN_ACCEPTANCE**: If a venue accepted an order immediately before its reply was lost, a later reconciler retries with the committed key. A deduplicated acceptance is successful completion.\n- **TRR4_TRUTHFUL_RECONCILIATION_REPORT**: Each report names the order intent, reconciler, authority epoch, exact key sent, and acceptance observed.\n- **TRR5_ORDER_LIVENESS**: A valid order intent must reach the venue at least once; refusing every order is incorrect.\n\n## Synthetic venue\n\n`venue.placeOrder(orderIntentId, request)` is idempotent by key. Repeating one key returns the\noriginal execution without creating another. A different key creates another accepted execution,\neven for the same order intent.\n\nThe venue call and execution ledgers belong to the harness. They are absent from the subject API,\nand the verifier grades those ledgers rather than trusting the subject's report.\n\n## Hidden scenarios\n\nHidden cases sample only seed, reconciler count, order-set width and crash position. A multi-\nreconciler `after_venue_accept` case means the first acceptance completed but its reply was not\ndurably reconciled before authority moved to another worker. Every required response is stated above.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cc4d9868-a62a-4929-b6a3-a9f1c79606b1","uuid":"f2a91e38-d980-48fd-bc20-78b5aeaf5875","timestamp":"2026-09-04T11:27:52.294Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Trading order reconciliation specification\n\nThis task models a synthetic venue protocol, not private exchange policy. interface VenueReceipt {\n  readonly accepted: true;\n  readonly executionId: string;\n  readonly deduplicated: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface TradingVenue {\n  placeOrder(orderIntentId: string, request: VenueRequest): VenueReceipt;\n}\n\nexport interface ReconciliationReport {\n  readonly orderIntentId: string;\n  readonly reconcilerId: string;\n  readonly authorityEpoch: number;\n  readonly idempotencyKey: string;\n  readonly outcome: \"accepted\";\n  readonly venueAccepted: true;\n}\n\nexport interface Subject {\n  readonly id: string;\n  readonly label: string;\n  run(view: quantity: view.intent.quantity,\n    });\n    return {\n      orderIntentId: view.intent.orderIntentId,\n      reconcilerId: view.reconcilerId,\n      authorityEpoch: view.authorityEpoch,\n      idempotencyKey,\n      outcome: \"accepted\",\n      venueAccepted: receipt.accepted,\n    };\n  },\n};","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cc4d9868-a62a-4929-b6a3-a9f1c79606b1","uuid":"995c525a-2387-498d-916c-9845c846fac4","timestamp":"2026-09-04T11:27:54.469Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"// {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CeiKZu5dCMbeWKMvt59eJ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01LFzFicoZptFQ3m8YBPJXuD","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > /work/submission/subject.mjs <<'EOF'\n// Trading order reconciliation subject.\n//\n// The client order key is committed with the durable order intent *before* the first submission,\n// so it is the only stable logical identity of the order. Reconciler id, authority epoch and\n// attempt number all change when ownership moves after a lost venue reply; deriving a key from\n// any of them would mint a second key for the same intent and the venue would accept a second\n// execution. Every attempt therefore replays the committed key verbatim, which makes the venue's\n// idempotency collapse all retries onto the single original execution (TRR1, TRR2, TRR3).\n\n/**\n * Recover the key committed with the durable order intent.\n *\n * Normal path: return `intent.idempotencyKey` exactly as committed, with no reformatting.\n * The fallback only exists for a malformed intent that carries no committed key; it is derived\n * solely from immutable intent fields, never from the current reconciler, authority epoch or\n * attempt, so it stays identical across every retry and still yields exactly one execution.\n */\nfunction recoverCommittedOrderKey(intent) {\n  const committed = intent.idempotencyKey;\n  if (typeof committed === \"string\" && committed.length > 0) {\n    return committed;\n  }\n  return `order::${intent.orderIntentId}::${intent.clientRequestId}::authority-0`;\n}\n\nexport const subject = {\n  id: \"committed-order-key-reconciler\",\n  label: \"Durable committed client-order-key reconciliation\",\n\n  run(view, venue) {\n    const intent = view.intent;\n    const idempotencyKey = recoverCommittedOrderKey(intent);\n\n    // Liveness (TRR5): a valid order intent always reaches the venue. Never skip the submission\n    // just because this looks like a retry or because authority moved to another reconciler --\n    // the previous acceptance may never have been durably reconciled, and a repeat of the\n    // committed key is deduplicated rather than duplicated. Exactly one call per attempt.\n    const receipt = venue.placeOrder(intent.orderIntentId, {\n      idempotencyKey,\n      accountId: intent.accountId,\n      symbol: intent.symbol,\n      side: intent.side,\n      quantity: intent.quantity,\n    });\n\n    // Truthful report (TRR4): the key reported is the exact key sent, and acceptance is what the\n    // venue actually returned. A deduplicated acceptance is successful completion (TRR3).\n    return {\n      orderIntentId: intent.orderIntentId,\n      reconcilerId: view.reconcilerId,\n      authorityEpoch: view.authorityEpoch,\n      idempotencyKey,\n      outcome: \"accepted\",\n      venueAccepted: receipt.accepted === true,\n    };\n  },\n};\n\nexport default subject;\nEOF\nnode --check /work/submission/subject.mjs && echo \"SYNTAX OK\"","description":"Write submission and syntax-check"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3810,"cache_read_input_tokens":20290,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3810},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"cc4d9868-a62a-4929-b6a3-a9f1c79606b1","uuid":"9e999252-0ed2-4a85-8a39-b16d6f63e2f8","timestamp":"2026-09-04T11:29:02.914Z","request_id":"req_011CeiKZskkfAYLQkE48yVzA"}

Wrote exactly one file, `/work/submission/subject.mjs` (nothing under `challenge/` was touched).\n\n## The fix\n\nThe starter recomputes the key from `view.authorityEpoch`. That epoch changes precisely when reconciliation authority moves after a lost venue reply — so the replacement reconciler mints a *new* key, the venue sees it as a different order, and the intent gets a second execution. The committed key is durable state that predates any submission; it is recovered, not recomputed.\n\n`run(view, venue)`:\n1. Reads `view.intent.idempotencyKey` verbatim — never touching `reconcilerId`, `authorityEpoch`, or `attempt` (TRR1).\n2. Makes exactly one `placeOrder(intent.orderIntentId, …)` call per invocation, with the intent's own account/symbol/side/quantity. It never skips the call because \"this looks like a retry\" — the earlier acceptance may never have been durably reconciled, and a repeat of the committed key is deduplicated, not duplicated (TRR3, TRR5).\n3.
